references.text: Here we see the same title 'Son of Man' who receives judgment authority, just as in John 5:27. In Daniel's vision, one like a son of man is given an eternal kingdom and judgment power from the Ancient of Days.
Psalm 110:1 links the Messiah to sitting at God's right hand and having his enemies made his footstool, which presupposes the judgment authority given to the Son of Man in John 5:27.
Isaiah describes how God's righteousness and judgment will come to the nations, reflecting Jesus' role as the appointed judge in John 5:27.
In Matthew 25, Jesus describes his second coming where he, as the Son of Man, will sit on his holy throne and judge all nations, a direct extension of the authority given in John 5:27.
Revelation confirms that the Son of Man comes with the clouds, and everyone will see him, including those who pierced him, and he will judge, fulfilling the authority given in John 5:27.

In the same book, Jesus confirms that he is the one who will judge, and that he does not judge on his own but according to the Father's will, emphasizing the source of the power mentioned in John 5:27.
